title: A coplanar third star of 0.253 solar masses fits 31 eclipse times of ASAS J090232-5653.4
abstract: A light-travel-time fit of ASAS J090232-5653.4 gave a third-star mass function of 0.443 solar masses. We test whether its timing data require a massive third star. One exact Newtonian state with a coplanar third star of 0.253 solar masses fits 19 TESS eclipse times and 12 ASAS-3 timing measurements with chi-square 26.78. The stellar masses and common inclination are fixed to published spectroscopic and eclipse values. The outer period is 1462.75 days and its initial eccentricity is 0.60. The source pure light-delay fit has chi-square 15.30 and would require at least 2.244 solar masses at the same pair mass. The light-companion timing state also gives chi-square 30.34 for 22 published 2014 velocities after two velocity zero points are fitted. A separate barycentre test shows that the short velocity run does not select either timing mechanism. Two finite 10000-year integrations retain the light-companion state. The result is a physical counterexample to a robust large mass limit, not a mass measurement or a global orbit fit. Fixed stellar masses, coplanar geometry, a selected outer state, reused timing estimates, omitted stellar forces and the short velocity baseline limit the result. Code, state, hashes, external-data retrieval scripts, aggregate checks and conditional velocity forecasts are included.
